blocks.text: Scalability algorithm ki woh ability hai ke input data ka size barhne par bhi us ki efficiency qaim rahe. Jo algorithm achhi tarah scale karta hai woh tab bhi efficiently chalta hai jab input data us size se kahin zyada ho jis ke liye woh shuru mein banaya gaya tha.

blocks.prompt: Binary search linear search se behtar scale kyun karti hai?
blocks.explanation: Binary search ka waqt log n ki tarah barhta hai: das lakh (1,000,000) tarteeb wali cheezon mein sirf taqreeban 20 jaanchein (2²⁰ ≈ 10 lakh), jabke linear search ko das lakh jaanchein lag sakti hain.

blocks.text: Yeh program sorted list ke size ke liye worst case (sab se buri soorat) mein Linear Search aur Binary Search ki jaanchein (checks) ginta hai. size badal kar Run karein aur dekhein kaunsa behtar scale karta hai.

size = 1000000   # number of sorted items

def binary_checks(n):
    checks = 0
    while n > 0:
        n = n // 2        # each check throws away half
        checks += 1
    return checks

print("Items:", size)
print("Linear Search, worst case:", size, "checks")
print("Binary Search, worst case:", binary_checks(size), "checks")

items: Scalable algorithm input bohat barhne par bhi efficient rehta hai.
